sourcedFrom: RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM182) — PM182, DH 11/2024 R16 (2024 (© 2024 Sturm, Ruger & Co., Inc.))
cleanIntro: The Hawkeye African is a hinged-FLOORPLATE Mauser-pattern bolt rifle, and Ruger's own book for it names it on the cover alongside the Hunter and the Guide Gun. ⛔ Routine cleaning needs only two things opened: the bolt out, and the floorplate down. The one part Ruger tells you never to take apart is the FIRING PIN ASSEMBLY — it is a permanent assembly under great spring pressure. ⚠ And the African carries express sights the other Hawkeyes do not, with their own adjustment procedure in this book.

steps.title: Safety to LOAD-UNLOAD, then prove chamber AND magazine empty
steps.action: Keep the rifle pointed in a safe direction and put the safety in the "Load-Unload" position — on this rifle the bolt will not open on full SAFE. Then check, by eye, that the chamber AND the magazine are empty.
steps.prose: The middle safety position exists precisely so the rifle can be unloaded without ever being on FIRE. Use it.
steps.aside: 2. CHECK TO BE CERTAIN THAT THE CHAMBER AND MAGAZINE ARE EMPTY.
steps.quote: 1. Keep the rifle pointed in a safe direction! Put the safety in the “Load-Unload” position.
steps.cite: RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM182) — PM182, DH 11/2024 R16 — Disassembly, step 1, p.20

steps.title: Bolt out — pull back and PIVOT THE BOLT STOP open together
steps.action: Open the bolt and pull it to the rear while at the same time pivoting the bolt stop open. It is on the LEFT side of the receiver on a right-handed rifle. Two motions at once — the bolt will not clear until the stop is swung out of its path.
steps.prose: This is the whole field strip on a Hawkeye. Everything past it is optional.
steps.quote: To remove the bolt: Open bolt and pull to the rear while at the same time pivoting open the bolt stop which is located on the left side of the receiver on the right-handed version
steps.cite: RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM182) — PM182, DH 11/2024 R16 — Disassembly, step 3, p.20

steps.title: ⛔ Do NOT disassemble the firing pin assembly
steps.action: The firing pin assembly can be taken OUT of the bolt — a pin or nail through the "disassembly hole" in the cocking piece — but it must not be taken APART. Ruger states it is intended to be a permanent assembly, that the parts are under great spring pressure, and that they could fly apart with enough force to cause serious injury.
steps.prose: Out of the bolt for cleaning is fine. Opened up on the bench is not, and Ruger says why.
steps.quote: To remove firing pin assembly from bolt: With bolt out of the rifle and firing pin cocked, insert a pin or nail into the “disassembly hole” in the cocking piece.
steps.cite: RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM182) — PM182, DH 11/2024 R16 — Disassembly, step 4, p.20
steps.warn: CAUTION: The firing pin assembly is intended to be a permanent assembly and should not be disassembled. The parts are under great spring pressure and if disassembled could fly apart with sufficient force to cause serious injury.

steps.title: Stock off — open the FLOORPLATE first, then the front mounting screw
steps.action: Open the floorplate and hold it up out of the way, then loosen and remove the front mounting screw that holds the floorplate hinge assembly. ⚠ The floorplate is what gives you access to that screw — this is a floorplate rifle, and the order is not optional.
steps.prose: If you have looked for a magazine well on this rifle, that is why: there is a hinged floorplate instead, and it is part of the strip.
steps.quote: To remove stock: Open floorplate and while holding it up out of the way, loosen and remove the front mounting screw
steps.cite: RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM182) — PM182, DH 11/2024 R16 — Disassembly, step 5, p.21

steps.title: ⚠ Routine cleaning needs only the BOLT OUT and the FLOORPLATE OPEN
steps.action: Ruger's own scope for routine work: remove the bolt and open the floorplate, and that is all the disassembly cleaning requires. ⛔ Before any of it, be certain the rifle and its magazine are unloaded.
steps.prose: Everything in the strip above beyond the bolt is for a reason other than cleaning. Knowing that saves an evening.
steps.quote: 1. For routine cleaning it is necessary only to remove the bolt and open the floorplate.
steps.cite: RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM182) — PM182, DH 11/2024 R16 — Care and Cleaning, step 1, p.24
steps.warn: WARNING: BEFORE CLEANING, BE CERTAIN THE RIFLE AND ITS MAGAZINE ARE UNLOADED.

steps.title: Bore: push-pull a solvent patch, then a bristle brush full length
steps.action: Push-pull a properly sized, solvent-wetted patch through the bore several times. Then put a solvent-wetted bristle brush on the rod and run it back and forth the full length of the bore until the fouling is out.
steps.prose: Full length matters: stopping short leaves the brush's turnaround point as a ring of fouling that never moves.
steps.quote: 2. Push-pull a properly sized, solvent-wetted patch through the bore several times.
steps.cite: RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM182) — PM182, DH 11/2024 R16 — Care and Cleaning, step 2, p.24

steps.title: Receiver: solvent patch on every REACHABLE surface, toothbrush for caked dirt
steps.action: Use a clean solvent-wetted patch to take firing residue and dirt off all the reachable surfaces inside the receiver, and a solvent-wetted toothbrush to dislodge caked dirt from anything the patch cannot follow.
steps.prose: "Reachable" is Ruger's own word and it is an honest one — this is a rifle you clean without opening the action further.
steps.quote: 3. Use a clean, solvent-wetted patch to remove firing residue and dirt from all “reachable” surfaces inside the receiver.
steps.cite: RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM182) — PM182, DH 11/2024 R16 — Care and Cleaning, step 3, p.24

steps.title: ⚠ A VERY LIGHT coat of oil — because oil COLLECTS dirt
steps.action: Wipe all surfaces, internal and external, with a VERY LIGHT coat of oil. Ruger gives the reason in the same sentence: oil and similar preparations collect dirt particles, and those interfere with reliable functioning.
steps.prose: This is the sentence that separates a protected rifle from a lapping compound in the receiver.
steps.quote: Wipe all surfaces – internal and external – with a very light coat of oil.
steps.cite: RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM182) — PM182, DH 11/2024 R16 — Care and Cleaning, step 4, p.24

steps.title: ⛔ ACETONE SOLVENTS CAN DAMAGE THE STOCK FINISH
steps.action: Keep cleaning solvents containing acetone off the stock. Ruger names the hazard specifically for camo-dipped patterns, which acetone will lift. Wipe all solvent, lubricating and preservative preparations off the stock when the rifle goes back together.
steps.prose: A wood or dipped stock is the part of this rifle a solvent ruins permanently, and it is the part nobody thinks of as a cleaning surface.
steps.aside: Reassemble the rifle and carefully wipe all solvent, lubricating and preservative preparations from the stock.
steps.quote: NOTE: Use of cleaning solvents containing acetone can damage the finish of your stock, particularly if your stock has a camo-dipped pattern.
steps.cite: RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM182) — PM182, DH 11/2024 R16 — Care and Cleaning, p.24

deepSteps.title: ⚠ AFRICAN-ONLY — the express sights have their own procedure
deepSteps.action: The African and the Guide Gun are the models in this book with a fixed elevation rear sight, set for approximately 50 yards, and Ruger gives them their own sight section. Windage is adjusted laterally at the rear sight; the elevation is not a user adjustment on these models.
deepSteps.prose: Included because it is the one place this book treats the African as its own rifle rather than one of a family.
deepSteps.quote: Both the Ruger “African” and Guide Gun bolt action rifles are equipped with a fixed elevation rear sight set for approximately 50 yards.
deepSteps.cite: RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM182) — PM182, DH 11/2024 R16 — Sight Picture and Adjustment for “African” and Guide Gun Models Only, p.26

deepSteps.title: ⛔ A lost spring or plunger is NOT substituted
deepSteps.action: Before you start taking the action apart, know Ruger's rule: if a spring or plunger becomes lost, do NOT use a substitute. Spring tension is a safety property on a firearm, and a hardware-store spring of the right size is not the right spring.
deepSteps.prose: Work over a covered bench — Ruger recommends a shallow nap rug or an old coarse blanket, precisely so a plunger that escapes is still findable.
deepSteps.quote: If a spring or plunger becomes lost do not use a substitute. Springs of correct tension are vital to the safe and reliable performance of firearms.
deepSteps.cite: RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM182) — PM182, DH 11/2024 R16 — Disassembly — Warning, p.20

deepSteps.title: Long-term storage — strip it, and put the small parts somewhere
deepSteps.action: If the rifle is going away for an extended period, clean it thoroughly and disassemble it to the extent this manual describes, taking care to put pins and similar easily mislaid parts somewhere they will be found again.
deepSteps.prose: The storage instruction is also the reminder that this manual bounds its own depth — "to the extent described elsewhere in this manual".
deepSteps.quote: 6. If the rifle is to be stored for an extended period, clean the rifle thoroughly.
deepSteps.cite: RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES INSTRUCTION MANUAL (PM182) — PM182, DH 11/2024 R16 — Care and Cleaning, step 6, p.24

cleaning.name: ROUTINE — BOLT OUT, FLOORPLATE OPEN
tasks: Rifle and magazine confirmed unloaded first
Solvent-wetted patch push-pulled through the bore several times
Solvent-wetted bristle brush the FULL length of the bore
Clean solvent patch over every reachable surface in the receiver

cleaning.name: OIL AND STOCK
tasks: VERY LIGHT coat of oil, internal and external — oil collects dirt
⛔ No acetone-bearing solvent near the stock finish
All solvent, lubricant and preservative wiped off the stock on reassembly

cleaning.name: LEAVE ALONE
tasks: ⛔ The firing pin assembly is permanent — out of the bolt, never apart
⛔ A lost spring or plunger is replaced with the correct part, never a substitute

reassembly: Firing pin assembly back into the bolt, intact.
Stock on; front mounting screw and floorplate hinge assembly seated.
Bolt in with the bolt stop pivoted clear, then closed and cycled.
All solvent and oil wiped off the stock.
Safety cycled through its positions on an empty chamber.
fncheck: With the chamber and magazine confirmed empty: cycle the bolt through full travel and check it locks and unlocks cleanly, and that the bolt stop retains it at the rear. Work the three-position safety and confirm the middle "Load-Unload" position lets the bolt open while the trigger stays blocked. Open and close the floorplate and confirm it latches. ⛔ Confirm the bore is clear of patches, brush bristles and oil before any live round — Ruger warns that oil or grease even partially obstructing the bore can damage the rifle and injure the shooter.
